content:
Apple is carrying out an extended testing period for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, currently rolling out the seventh candidate release for both systems. Here are the latest details.

The new release candidate is now available

Four days ago, Apple released the sixth release candidate of macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, along with the first release candidate of macOS 26.6 and its corresponding versions.

Given the timeframe and the number of release candidates, one would naturally assume these are the final testing versions before the official release. In fact, that is not the case.

Apple today released the seventh release candidate of macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, with the following build numbers:

  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 (23J620)
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 (24G824)

Both versions are now available for download by developers and public beta testers.

Apple has not yet specified the contents of these two systems, only stating as usual that "this update provides important security fixes and is recommended for all users to install." Apple will most likely provide more details on its Apple security updates webpage after the two systems are officially released.

Apple has always released updates for older system versions, providing important bug fixes for users who are unable to run the latest software. The current situation is believed to be no exception, so any users still using macOS Sonoma or Sequoia should install the update as soon as possible after it is publicly released, which is expected to be as early as the beginning of next week.
